newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay says all A330s in air by weekend. [CORRECTED 14:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cathay says all A330s in air by weekend. [CORRECTED 14:20 GMT]

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its fleet of 11 Airbus Industrie A330-300 aircraft to be flying again by this weekend after they were grounded since May 24 with engine trouble.
"We're confident that we will have the entire fleet flying by the weekend," engineering director Roland Fairfield told a news conference.
Fairfield said the weekend deadline was an update to a statement issued earlier on Thursday.
That statement said the first A330-300 with modified engines would re-enter service on Thursday morning, with the rest of the fleet to return to service "over the next week".
The first A330-300 would resume service on Thursday as announced in the statement, Cathay Pacific officials said.

Cathay Pacific suspended its entire fleet of A330-300s on May 24 after three inflight engine shutdowns and a fourth on a Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd (Dragonair) A330-300 created questions about the reliability of the Rolls-Royce Plc Trent 700 engine.
The engine problems stem from the lubrication system used in the Trent 700 gearbox, Rolls-Royce says.
Dragonair, 25.5 percent owned by Cathay Pacific and Swire Pacific Ltd, also suspended its four A330-300s.
Dragonair said on Wednesday it expected the first of its A330-300s to resume flying on Thursday morning.

(Corrects to delete paragraph containing company statement which said some of the planes may not be in service until next week. All of the planes are now expected to be in service by the end of this week.)
